==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|custumer}}, from {{der|en|fro|coustumier}}, {{m|fro|costumier}} (compare modern French {{m|fr|coutumier}}), from {{der|en|la-med|custumarius||a toll-gatherer, tax-collector|pos=noun}}, from {{m|la|custumarius||pertaining to custom or customs|pos=adjective}}, from {{m|la|custuma||custom, tax}}. More at {{m|en|custom}}. {{surf|en|custom|-er|id2=occupation}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌs.tə.mə/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-customer.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌs.tə.mɚ/|a=GA.CA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɐs.tə.mə/|a=AU,NZ}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[habitual]] [[patron]], [[regular]] [[purchaser]], [[returning]] [[client]]; a [[person]] or [[company]] who has a [[custom]] of buying from a particular business.
# A [[person]] or [[company]] who [[purchase]]s or [[receive]]s a [[product]] or [[service]] from a [[business]] or [[merchant]] or intends to do so.
#: {{syn|en|patron|client|solicitor}}
#: {{ux|en|Every person who passes by is a potential '''customer'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Airlines are the chief '''customers''' of the commercial divisions of large-aircraft manufacturers such as Airbus, Boeing, and Embraer.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A person, especially one engaging in some sort of [[interaction]] with others.
#: ''a cool '''customer''''', ''a tough '''customer''''', ''an ugly '''customer'''''
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1971|author=w:Herman Wouk|chapter=52
|title=The Winds of War
|passage=''Pug could just see Slote's pale face under his fur hat.  "I don't agree with you on that.  He's a pretty tough '''customer''', Hopkins."''}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020 January 2|author=Philip Haigh|title=Ten eventful years and plenty of talking points|journal=Rail|page=54|text=This switch led to Philip Hammond becoming the Transport Secretary and he quickly proved to be a tricky '''customer''', asking questions about rail spending and reining it back whenever possible.}}
# {{lb|en|India|historical}} A [[native]] [[official]] who [[exact]]ed [[customs]] [[duty|duties]]. <!--for full citation sources, see Hobson-Jobson 1903-->
#*: His houses {{...}} are seized on by the '''Customer'''.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1615|author=Sir T. Roe|title=Hak. Soc. i. 44
|passage=The '''Customer''' should come and visit them.}}
